statement: For a total-revenue question, aggregate the approved revenue measure over the requested filters in SQL, then validate the scalar result.
validation_rule: Confirm the revenue definition and date/status filters before execution.

statement: For monthly/weekly/daily revenue, aggregate the approved revenue measure at the requested time grain in SQL and return one row per period.
formula: Period revenue = SUM(revenue) GROUP BY requested period
required_inputs: revenue expression; date field; time grain; filters
validation_rule: Check that each record belongs to exactly one requested period and periods are ordered chronologically.

statement: Calculate period-over-period growth deterministically after retrieving verified period totals.
required_inputs: current period value; previous period value
validation_rule: Previous value must be nonzero; periods must be comparable and adjacent under the requested definition.

statement: Use CAGR only for multi-period compounded growth and disclose that it can mask individual year-to-year variation.
required_inputs: starting value; ending value; N periods
validation_rule: Starting value must be positive for the standard formula; state N and unit.

statement: For top products/customers/categories, aggregate the target measure at the entity grain and rank descending; apply a deterministic tie rule.
validation_rule: Verify the aggregation grain and tie-handling; do not rank raw transaction rows.

statement: Average order value should be computed from verified order-level revenue divided by the count of included orders, not from an average of line-item values.
formula: AOV = Total included order revenue / Included order count
validation_rule: Build/verify order grain first; denominator must be nonzero.

statement: Compute an entity contribution share by dividing its verified measure by the verified total for the same scope.
validation_rule: Numerator and denominator must use identical filters/time scope; total must be nonzero.

statement: Calculate NPS from survey classifications only when promoter and detractor percentages are available for the same population.
validation_rule: Result must be within -100 to 100; do not infer NPS from ratings without the defined classification rule.

statement: Use the constant-retention CLV formula only when its assumptions fit the requested analysis.
validation_rule: Same time unit; valid denominator; disclose constant-margin/retention assumptions.

statement: Compute average acquisition cost as total acquisition spending divided by newly acquired customers for the same campaign/period.
formula: AAC = Acquisition spending / New customers acquired
validation_rule: Acquired customer count > 0 and scope aligned.

statement: Estimate price elasticity from comparable percentage changes in quantity demanded and price when the data support such an inference.
required_inputs: price observations; quantity observations; comparable context
validation_rule: Do not infer causality from uncontrolled before/after data; disclose estimation basis.

statement: For a defensible linear-demand model, compute contribution-maximizing price as the midpoint between maximum reservation price and variable cost.
validation_rule: Use only for a linear demand function; otherwise mark method unsupported.

statement: Use contribution per unit to separate variable economics from fixed costs.
required_inputs: price per unit; variable cost per unit
validation_rule: Inputs must use the same unit and currency basis.

statement: Compute break-even volume from fixed cost and positive contribution per unit under constant cost/price assumptions.
formula: Break-even volume = Fixed cost / (Price - Variable cost)
required_inputs: fixed cost; unit price; unit variable cost
validation_rule: Contribution per unit must be > 0; disclose model assumptions.

statement: Discount each project cash flow at the required rate for its period and sum, including the initial investment.
validation_rule: Rate and cash-flow periods must align; include t=0 correctly.

statement: Compute IRR deterministically as a root of the NPV function, while checking for nonconventional cash flows and ambiguous roots.
validation_rule: If multiple sign changes or no stable root, flag IRR as ambiguous/unavailable and prioritize NPV.

statement: Compute productivity as output divided by the chosen input; state whether the measure is labor, machine, material, or multifactor productivity.
validation_rule: Numerator/denominator must use compatible scope and period; denominator > 0.

statement: Compute utilization as actual output divided by design capacity for the same period.
validation_rule: Design capacity > 0 and same output/time unit.

statement: Calculate inventory turnover using the organization's approved numerator/average-inventory convention and state that convention.
validation_rule: Do not compare turnover values computed with different conventions or periods.

statement: Use the approved reorder-point policy for independent-demand items and include safety stock when the selected policy requires it.
required_inputs: demand rate; lead time; safety stock/policy
validation_rule: Demand and lead-time units must align; never invent safety stock.

statement: For exploratory numeric summaries, use deterministic counts, central tendency, dispersion, quantiles, and grouped summaries before explanatory conclusions.
validation_rule: Report missing-value handling and avoid extrapolating beyond observed data.

statement: Use root-cause methods to investigate why a problem occurs after the problem is evidenced; do not label the first plausible explanation as the root cause.
validation_rule: Require evidence that discriminates among candidate causes.

statement: For external-environment questions, organize evidence under PESTLE categories and keep the output qualitative unless measured data are available.
validation_rule: No fabricated force scores; label dated/geographic evidence.

statement: For industry-structure questions, organize evidence around entrants, substitutes, buyer power, supplier power, and rivalry.
validation_rule: Do not translate narrative evidence into numeric attractiveness scores unless an approved scoring model is provided.

statement: When a business query is unexpectedly slow, inspect EXPLAIN/access type and rows examined before proposing optimization.
validation_rule: Runtime may diagnose but must not alter schema/indexes automatically.

statement: Use a line chart for ordered time trends when the primary question concerns change over time; keep the underlying table available for audit.
validation_rule: Periods must be sorted and complete/explicitly missing; chart values must match the verified table.

statement: Use a bar chart for discrete category comparisons when length comparison communicates the result more clearly than a table.
validation_rule: Sort intentionally when useful; preserve exact values in supporting table.

statement: After exploratory analysis, communicate the decision-relevant message rather than dumping every tested view.
validation_rule: Every headline statement must be supported by displayed or auditable evidence.
